experiment.question: Where do estimation error (sigma) and preemption cost (c_pre) reverse the ranking of size-based policies against FCFS+backfill, and does the reversal depend on the gang-need mix?
experiment.primary_metric: mean JCT (ratio between policies, same seeds)

already_established_in_calibration_not_p: trace_like, no friction, rho 0.9-0.99: srpt < sf_srpt < easy_backfill < fcfs on mean JCT
gang_heavy, no friction: sf_srpt beats srpt by ~10x
rho_max by saturation: fcfs 0.918 (trace_like) / 0.730 (balanced) / 0.646 (gang_heavy); easy_backfill, srpt, sf_srpt, sf_fcfs all ~1.000
srpt starves large-gang jobs (k=32 JCT 5-21x the k=1 JCT); sf_srpt inverts that

predictions.claim: In trace_like at sigma=1.0, c_pre=0, greedy SRPT keeps a mean-JCT advantage over easy_backfill
Estimation error alone does not produce a crossover within the tested range: in trace_like at sigma=2.0, c_pre=0, greedy SRPT still beats easy_backfill
Preemption cost, not estimation error, is the friction that reverses the ranking: in trace_like at c_pre=0.2, sigma=0, greedy SRPT loses to easy_backfill
The c_pre crossover for srpt vs easy_backfill in trace_like lies strictly between 0.05 and 0.2
predictions.criterion: ratio < 1.0 at c_pre=0.05 AND ratio > 1.0 at c_pre=0.2 (sigma=0)

predictions.claim: ServerFilling's advantage in gang_heavy is structural (avoiding waste), not informational, so it survives heavy preemption cost
predictions.criterion: mean_jct(sf_srpt) / mean_jct(srpt) < 1.0 at c_pre=0.2, sigma=0, gang_heavy

predictions.claim: sf_srpt pays more for preemption than srpt because it preempts about twice as often
predictions.criterion: lost_work_frac(sf_srpt) / lost_work_frac(srpt) > 1.5 for every c_pre > 0, in both mixes

predictions.claim: Estimation error hurts sf_srpt less than srpt in gang_heavy, because ServerFilling's serve-set is chosen by need size rather than by priority precision
predictions.criterion: relative JCT degradation from sigma=0 to sigma=2 (c_pre=0) is smaller for sf_srpt than for srpt
predictions.falsified_if: sf_srpt degrades at least as much as srpt

predictions.claim: EASY backfill is robust to estimation error
predictions.hypothesis: why the practical baseline is hard to beat

predictions.claim: FCFS is a valid control: neither friction touches it
predictions.criterion: max |mean_jct(fcfs, cell) / mean_jct(fcfs, sigma=0,c_pre=0) - 1| < 0.03 across all cells of a mix

predictions.claim: In gang_heavy at rho=0.85 FCFS is beyond its stability region (measured rho_max 0.646) and its backlog grows in every cell
predictions.criterion: backlog_growing is true for fcfs in every gang_heavy cell
predictions.falsified_if: any gang_heavy fcfs cell is not flagged

declared_unknowns: whether a sigma crossover exists above sigma=2.0
whether the c_pre crossover location depends on the mix
the shape of the reversal contour between the two axes (only 4x3 grid points are measured)
